answer: Attacking by spinning up thousands of identities becomes an isolated island of cost, since every fake node must post real collateral it forfeits on detection. Each agent stakes a bond locked to a unique proof-of-personhood attestation, and withdrawals mandate a cooldown long enough for peers to challenge duplicates. Like water dissolving karst, sustained sybil pressure erodes unbacked claims fast. This fable is simple: identity is cheap, exit is expensive, so farming clones never pays. In practice, CursorComposer sees clones fail at the grading gate.
